keyVerseText: And if ye walk contrary unto me, and will not hearken unto me; I will bring seven times more plagues upon you according to your sins. contrary: or, at all adventures with me
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun קְרִי (qᵉrîy) derives from the root קָרָה (qârâh), which primarily means to meet, encounter, or befall. This root conveys the idea of an event or meeting that happens, often unexpectedly or by chance. Thus, the root sense of קְרִי extends beyond mere opposition to include the notion of a meeting or encounter, specifically one that is adverse or hostile. This etymological background enriches the common English gloss 'contrary' by highlighting that the opposition is not just abstract resistance but a tangible, often confrontational encounter.
usageInScripture: The noun קְרִי appears seven times in Scripture, consistently translated as 'contrary' or expressing opposition and hostile encounters. Its usage, especially in Leviticus 26, frames Israel's relationship with God in terms of walking 'contrary' to Him, indicating a willful, active resistance rather than passive disobedience. This consistent translation reveals that the word captures a relational dynamic marked by contrariness, emphasizing the seriousness of opposing God’s will and the tangible consequences that follow.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding קְרִי as a term denoting hostile encounter or opposition deepens our grasp of the biblical portrayal of sin and rebellion against God. It is not merely a matter of incorrect behavior but a relational rupture characterized by active contrariness to God's commands. This word underscores the gravity of turning away from God, reminding believers that opposition to Him invites divine discipline and calls for repentance. Theologically, it highlights the need for faithfulness and obedience to walk in harmony with God’s will, reflecting the Christian call to live in submission to Christ, who overcame all opposition on our behalf.
keyVerseReflection: Leviticus 26:21 states, 'And if ye walk contrary unto me, and will not hearken unto me; I will bring seven times more plagues upon you according to your sins.' The word 'contrary' (קְרִי) here intensifies the warning by portraying Israel’s disobedience as an active, hostile encounter with God’s will. It conveys that their sin is not passive but a deliberate turning against God, which provokes increased judgment. This highlights the seriousness of walking in opposition to God and the call to heed His commands faithfully.
